guides.title: Read-only protocol client
guides.summary: Discover a network, resolve canonical contracts, read chain state through the SDK, and use 420Indexer only for projection/query acceleration.

steps.action: Load and validate the selected network manifest and explicit chain ID.
Resolve the protocol address and verified interface from the selected catalogue.
Read security-relevant state from the selected chain through the shared SDK.
Use Indexer blocks, transactions, logs, protocol projections or search for developer UX and discovery.
Revalidate any security-sensitive decision against canonical chain/protocol state rather than an indexed projection.

guides.title: Wallet-aware transaction
guides.summary: Prepare a protocol interaction with the SDK and hand signing/submission to 420 Wallet or a qualified smart-account runtime.

steps.action: Bind the app to the selected network and canonical contract catalogue.
Encode the intended protocol call using the shared SDK/interface metadata.
Ask the qualified wallet runtime to evaluate account, chain and capability requirements.
Obtain explicit user/account authorization and submit through the wallet runtime. Developer Hub never handles raw signing secrets.
Confirm transaction inclusion/receipt from canonical RPC.
Use Indexer for subsequent history, logs and UI projections after canonical submission/confirmation.

guides.title: Deploy and verify a contract
guides.summary: Plan a non-custodial deployment, submit through an external signer, confirm it on-chain, then publish reproducible verification evidence to 420Verify.

steps.action: Produce the exact artifact, source bundle, compiler settings and hashes required for reproducibility.
Create a deployment plan bound to selected chain, canonical RPC, artifact provenance and public deployer identity.
Hand deployment execution to the declared external signer/executor. Developer Hub does not custody secrets.
Confirm transaction receipt, contract address and deployed runtime bytecode from canonical RPC.
Bind verification evidence to chain ID, address, runtime code hash, source bundle and compiler settings.
Submit reproducible evidence and preserve FULL_MATCH, PARTIAL_MATCH, MISMATCH or UNVERIFIABLE without treating verification as an audit or registration.

guides.title: Indexer diagnostics and query workflow
guides.summary: Use the public 420Indexer v1 API safely for health, readiness, status and developer queries without promoting projections into protocol authority.

steps.action: Resolve only the selected network's services.indexer endpoint and explicit chain ID.
Read health, readiness and chain-specific status; preserve readiness 503 as diagnostic data.
Use validated v1 queries, cursor pagination and structured errors for blocks, transactions, logs, transfers, protocol objects/events and search.
For authorization, settlement, governance, Registry legitimacy or wallet permissions, leave the Indexer projection and query the owning canonical authority.

guides.title: End-to-end dApp integration
guides.summary: Combine discovery, SDK reads, wallet-authorized writes, deployment, verification and Indexer UX while preserving every authority boundary.

steps.action: Discover the network, load canonical contracts and initialize the SDK.
Populate fast UI/search/history views from Indexer projections, visibly retaining source provenance.
Route any state-changing interaction through the qualified wallet/capability boundary.
Use the deployment planner and external signer flow for app-owned contracts; confirm receipt from canonical RPC.
Publish reproducible source/compiler evidence without equating verification with audit, safety or official status.

Validate the application release, perform canonical Registry preflight, hand publishRegisteredService to Registry governance, then project confirmed registration into the non-canonical AppStore catalogue.
